title: Quartz Solar AI Cloudcasting - predicting cloud movements through satellite imagery
summary: Open Climate Fix reports a 5% accuracy gain at a two-hour forecast horizon for a cloudcasting component awaiting Quartz Solar integration.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: An early cloudcasting evaluation reports a 5% accuracy gain at a two-hour horizon, with UK integration planned for summer 2025. The evaluation precedes the later Quartz Solar control-room deployment. Annual carbon savings remain projected.
purpose: Improve short-horizon solar forecasts through predicted satellite imagery.

ratings.reason: The cloudcasting evaluation reports a 5% accuracy improvement at a two-hour horizon before the later control-room deployment.
The 100,000-ton annual emissions saving is explicitly expected, not observed.

ai_role.statement: The account does not isolate AI’s contribution from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025). Project-submitted account, current as of June 2025. ITU provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 10: Quartz Solar AI Cloudcasting - predicting cloud movements through satellite imagery

produced_by: The account does not establish conditions sufficient to reproduce the benefit.
must_hold: The account does not establish requirements for reproducing the benefit in other settings.

headline: Cloudcasting improves a solar-forecast benchmark
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
